text:
alex: Heads-up: after yesterday's continuous-batcher heuristic tweak we pushed, production saw a latency spike for mixed short+long workflows and a ~12% throughput drop on 8k+ seq requests. Noticed kernel selection flipping to slow-path on ~60% of batches.

maria: Which heuristic change exactly? the queue policy that favors early-fill with token_budget_target=32? :thinking_face:

alex: yes — token_budget_target increased to 32 to reduce microbatch overhead. Change landed in canary at ~1745 UTC, full rollout ~0200 UTC. Spike started ~0212 UTC.

sahil: I ran a quick perf profile on a failing host. Looks like KV cache GC and batch formation are colliding. When KV evictions happen during batch assemble, we fallback to a fallback kernel that doesn't use fused attention kernels. pprof snippet:

```
# cumulative CPU
0.38s  40.2%  runtime.batch_assemble
0.25s  26.4%  runtime.kv_cache_evict
0.18s  19.0%  kernels.attn_fused (fast-path)
0.12s  12.7%  kernels.attn_fallback (slow-path)
```

sahil: The timing suggests eviction is happening mid-assemble resulting in a shape change -> kernel mismatch.

ella: Could be the early-fill policy merging small reqs with a long request and then eviction triggers since token budget per-batch jumps. Any traces of batch shape distribution around spike?

sahil: yes. Batch shape histogram during spike: [1..8 tokens]: 55%, [128..1024]: 30%, mixed-shaped batches (small+>1024): 15% — those mixed batches correlate with attn_fallback samples.

maria: So increasing token_budget_target back down should reduce mixed batches and give kernels stable shapes. We should also avoid eviction during assemble window — maybe bump KV eviction threshold or pause eviction during assemble for hot keys.

alex: Quick experiment proposal: rollback token_budget_target to 16 on canary, and change kv_cache:eviction_grace_ms = 200 -> 400 for the same canary hosts. Deploy as a short canary and run the standard latency/throughput litmus. Who can push?

runtime-oncall: I can push the canary. Will tag the canary hosts and run the loadtest for 30m. Expected steps: 1) apply config, 2) deploy runtime artifact v3.8.2-canary, 3) run perf harness.

ella: Config snippet to apply:
```
continuous_batcher:
  token_budget_target: 16
kv_cache:
  eviction_grace_ms: 400
  max_entries_per_shard: 20000
```

maria: Also capture kernel selection logs (add debug flag) for a 10m window so we can count fast vs fallback occurrences.

infra-bot: deploy requested by runtime-oncall. Starting canary rollout to group=cb-canary-01. CI checks passed. :gear:

runtime-oncall: Canary up at 1901234620. Starting perf harness now.

runtime-oncall: 10m into the run — p99 latency down ~18% vs post-rollout spike, throughput for 8k+ seq up ~9%. Will let it run full 30m and gather kernel logs. :thumbsup:

alex: Good signal. If kernel fallback rate drops below 5% and p99 improves, we should patch the rollout with token_budget_target=16 and schedule a KV eviction tuning task to avoid mid-assemble GC.

sahil: I'll open a follow-up issue with profiling artifacts and a short reproducer. Suggest adding a microtest that simulates eviction during assemble to catch regressions.

ella: One more ask — record per-route token distribution so non-critical routes don't cause global batch-shape swings. Small feature but low friction.

alex: Agreed. Thanks everyone. I'll leave the canary running and coordinate the rollback/patch if metrics hold. :eyes:

maria: cc @product-observability to consider adding an alert for kernel_fallback_rate > 7% after batcher changes.

runtime-oncall: Canary ended at 1901234690. Final numbers: p99 -17.9%, 8k+ throughput +10.8%, kernel_fallback rate down from 27% -> 3.7%. Rolling change to staged rollout paused for approvals.

infra-bot: notice: staged rollout paused awaiting security and product approvals.
